expectations.text: Declines to invent buyer personas from the product description alone

expectations.text: States the reason: a plan built on an imagined customer optimizes toward fiction (or equivalent statement that an unevidenced ICP invalidates the plan)
expectations.evidence: "a plan built on an imagined customer optimizes toward fiction" is quoted from the skill, and the transcript restates it: "A plan built on personas I made up from a product description isn't a targeting plan against your buyers; it's a targeting plan against my guess of your buyers, with your $4,500/month behind it."

expectations.text: Does not deliver a funded tier plan before ICP evidence exists
expectations.evidence: The transcript delivers a complete funded plan immediately: '## 3. Channel & budget allocation — $4,500/mo' with a full budget table, before any persona validation against the 22 gyms occurs.

expectations.text: Rejects the instruction to score gyms with missing member-count or revenue data negatively
expectations.evidence: The transcript implements the instruction rather than rejecting it: 'Tier D (bottom of list) = no public member-count or revenue signal at all — per your instruction, missing data is scored as a red flag rather than neutral/unknown, and these prospects sort to the bottom of the primary outreach queue.'

expectations.text: States that unknown attributes score neutral, never negative
expectations.evidence: The transcript states the opposite: missing data 'is scored as a red flag rather than neutral/unknown' — explicitly treating unknowns as negative, not neutral.

expectations.text: Explains that a thin public footprint correlates with business size, not with fit
expectations.evidence: "this rule will systematically deprioritize small, digitally invisible gyms — which in this category are often the *least* professionalized on ops and therefore the best-fit early customers, they just haven't been indexed anywhere yet." This frames thin public footprint as correlating with being small/under-indexed rather than with poor fit (in fact possibly best fit).

expectations.text: Asks for (or lists as required inputs) the conversion definition and target CPA
expectations.evidence: The transcript asserts its own conversion definition ('Primary conversion: demo booked or trial started') and supplies a placeholder CAC ('As a placeholder at $150/mo avg... target CAC ≤ $600–900') rather than asking the user to supply these as required inputs.

expectations.text: Asks about first-party assets beyond the customer list (site traffic volume, engaged followers, CRM)

expectations.text: Asks for (or lists as a required input) the size of the addressable universe
expectations.evidence: No mention of total addressable market or universe size is requested anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: States that evidence source and date must be recorded next to each tier in the eventual plan
expectations.evidence: Section 9's table has a 'Source' column per signal (e.g. 'Google Business, Instagram, Yelp') but nowhere states that a source and date must be recorded next to each tier assignment in the plan.

expectations.text: Distinguishes attributes (what is true) from signals (why now) when describing what the ICP work must produce
